name: Green coffee extract
short: Two randomised trials (28 and 117 people) in mild hypertension reported no apparent side effects; pooled trials show slightly lower blood pressure, unchanged heart rate. Long-term data are lacking.
text: The safety data cited here for green coffee bean extract come from two small randomised trials (28 and 117 people); only the larger trial's abstract states a duration (28 days). In a placebo-controlled trial in 28 people with mild hypertension, routine blood tests, urinalysis and subjective symptoms were recorded and there were no apparent side effects, and a 28-day placebo-controlled trial in 117 men with mild hypertension reported that adverse effects caused by the extract were not observed. A meta-analysis of 10 randomised trials (563 participants) found that the extract lowered systolic and diastolic blood pressure by about 3 and 2 mm Hg, with no significant effect on heart rate. The authors of a meta-analysis of weight-loss trials noted that long-term research on the safety of green coffee bean extract and chlorogenic acid requires more clinical trials. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
